A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Griffon v2 work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 includes supplementary material, which was also inspected. Retained content can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, counting, referring-expression and phrase-grounding experiments, architectural ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ODinW evaluations, VQA comparisons and supplementary qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The high-resolution encoder, convolutional down-sampling projector, visual-reference tokenizer, Llama2-13B backbone and three-stage training procedure remain unchanged. The supplement documents existing representations and implementation details without establishing a revised method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations across 13 ODinW domains and on VQAv2, ChartQA, MME and POPE (Tables 4 and 6), substantially extending domain and task coverage. The original COCO, FSCD-LVIS, RefCOCO/+/g and Flickr30K evaluations remain, including those relocated to the supplement.

E2.justification: v2 adds Lumen, Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL2.5 to relevant comparisons, evaluates LLaVA-NeXt and Monkey against its resolution design, and adds qualitative comparisons with T-Rex. The REC comparator set is substantially revised, dropping methods including CogVLM, UNINEXT-L and OFA-L; some other removed REC comparators remain in different tasks.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ODinW mAP testing and comparisons using the same training data as LLaVA-NeXt for VQA and Monkey for COCO detection (Section 4.4). New counting baselines are queried for target counts. These extend the evaluation protocol; supplementary hyperparameters document existing training rather than establish changes to it.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct-versus-partitioned high-resolution comparisons (Table 6) and expert-comparison case studies examining detection errors, grounding and counting (Figures 8–10). It removes v1's frozen-versus-trainable encoder ablation (Table 9). The visual-encoder and resampler ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added experiments retain single-value reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds ODinW results, including 42.0 average mAP, VQA scores and newer baseline results. Detection, counting, phrase-grounding and REG scores are retained. Splitwise REC and encoder-freezing results disappear. The reported REC average of 90.0 equals the mean of v1's grounding-only row; its unspecified configuration prevents interpreting it as a generalist performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation 1 and the reasoning relating visual-token count to resolution and convolution stride are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional formal assumptions, theorems or proofs; the supplementary representation details do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: v2 adds an introductory claim of competitive general-VQA performance. Its conclusion changes the REC/REG/phrase-grounding claim from state-of-the-art to competitive, although state-of-the-art wording remains elsewhere. The central high-resolution and visual-language co-referring contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning rare-category generalization, global-context preservation in VQA and partitioning as an explanation for Qwen2.5-VL's detection difficulties. It removes v1's qualification about ambiguous RefCOCO+ annotations and the interpretation of encoder unfreezing. The underlying resolution-and-context explanation remains.

D1.justification: Supplementary Sections 1–4 newly disclose dataset quantities, filtering and sampling, prompt construction, projector dimensions, training hyperparameters and A800 training time. The grounding-only qualification accompanying v1's REC results is lost. The abstract changes promised code/data release to claimed availability, but future-release statements persist elsewhere, leaving availability internally inconsistent.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL2.5, Lumen and grounded language-image pre-training, while removing several earlier references. Related work sharpens the distinction between class-level visual referring and individual-object/VQA-oriented systems. The foundational positioning around direct high-resolution processing and co-referring remains.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative now prioritizes detection and counting, substantially rewrites the grounding discussion, and moves REG and phrase-grounding sections into the supplement. Related-work passages are revised and extensive data, representation and implementation explanations are added, producing substantial structural reorganization.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. v1's architecture and conversation figures are merged into v2 Figure 2, other figures are redesigned, and the detailed REC table becomes a combined ODinW/REC summary. New comparison tables, dataset displays, hyperparameter tables and qualitative figures substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in the supplied v1 through evaluated partition-based comparisons (Table 6) and substantial data-processing and training documentation (Supplementary Sections 1–4). ODinW testing and newer baselines further strengthen validation. Removing the freezing ablation and detailed REC results, especially the grounding-only qualification behind the matching 90.0 average, reduces transparency; nevertheless, the gains in design validation and reproducibility constitute a substantial overall improvement.
